newsitem.title: USA: NYS gov wants to focus on getting budget in June.
newsitem.headline: NYS gov wants to focus on getting budget in June.

text.p: New York State Gov George Pataki on Monday said he wanted to focus on getting a budget done by June 20, when a second stop-gap pact ends, but cautioned that meeting this deadline would be hard.

Asked if the state, which for the 13th year in a row missed its April 1 budget deadline, would put a nine-month interim pact in place, Pataki told reporters in Albany: "When and if we are faced with the question of doing that, we'll look at it. Right now, my focus is to try to get things done by June 20. It's going to be difficult, but it's not impossible."
The Republican governor spoke to reporters after meeting with Senate Majority Leader, Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, and the Assembly Speaker, Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan.
They next are slated to meet on Wednesday. There appeared to be no progress in resolving one of the biggest stumbling blocks to reaching a budget--a heated fight over rent regulations for apartments.

Bruno, who wants the rules, which mainly affect New York City apartment dwellers, phased out and wants any bill to include "vacancy decontrol," again warned that the regulations would be allowed to end on June 15 when they expire if no agreement were reached.
"There will be no extensions in the Senate, not for five minutes," he vowed, one day before tenant avocate groups plan to demonstrate in Albany in favor of the rules.

But the Assembly Speaker showed no sign of retreating from his opposition to Pataki's plan, which would return apartments to the free market system once a tenant voluntarily moves or dies, a form of deregulation called vacancy decontrol, though Pataki has said his plan would keep the present rules for the elderly and disabled would be protected, along with the rules that let tenants inherit regulated apartments.

"That will always remain unacceptable to me. Vacancy decontrol is not the way to go, it's a failed policy of the past," Silver said. Assembly Democrats say an experiment with vacancy decontrol from 1971 to 1974 led landlords to try to push tenants out, and rent rules were reinstated.
